findings.reason: §2's proposal must be stated as settling whether that table becomes a graph class and how `field_code_meanings` in private configuration retires, not a fresh field-code mechanism.
findings.text: §1 problem 3 ("field-code meanings live in private configuration, not in the graph") is already built: `field_codes.py` and `field_codes_graph.py` assemble a per-code role-and-meaning table from three graph sources in precedence, `iter_codex/remote/field_code_table.py:1` stores it privately with a determinism assertion, and `ArchiveFieldPattern.description` (facility.yaml:2093) already says "Meaning of the shared fields when established from linked context". §2 will re-derive a mechanism whose hard parts (precedence, conflict recording, per-component-kind keys, the empty-source-must-raise check in `field_codes_graph.py:8`) exist and are tested

findings.reason: the section's "catalogued-document form" is largely the existing receipt plus two fields, and saying so changes what §3 must define and what §4 must write.
findings.text: §4 asks for documents with identity, title, current version, version state, file type and sheets; `ICPDocuments.fetch` already returns a `DocumentReceipt` carrying `uid`, `version`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `page_count` (facility.yaml-unrelated but documents.py:13-28) and `sheets`, i.e. every identity field §4 needs except version state and PBS references. The plan's §4 text does not say it extends this receipt shape

findings.reason: §4 now rests on a capability that is designed out, and the plan must either add a bounded search endpoint to the client or state that the export is the only route and why.
findings.text: §4 says document records are read "through the project's read-only client, or through a record export the coordinator supplies where that client cannot search". `records.py:4-5 says list-view and query POST operations are deliberately absent from this reader"` and `icp/client.py:198` refuses every POST but sign-in, so the search §4 depends on cannot run through the client as written; §4 does not say this and offers the export as though it were an equivalent instrument. The same traversal is also already proven in the graph for the signal→row→PBS join (`vocabulary_graph.py:62`, `SignalContextLink` at facility.yaml:1940)

findings.reason: the settled answer may be a stated precedence between two axes rather than one vocabulary, and §2 asks for one vocabulary, which would change what §3 has to migrate and what domain_queries must accept.
findings.text: §1 problem 1 says the two role vocabularies have "no statement of which is canonical", but `SignalRole` (185, six values, judged from prose, model) and `SignalVocabularyRole` (271, five values, assigned by rule from a source) are documented as deliberately orthogonal, and both are queried as separate predicates in `iter_codex/graph/domain_queries.py:150` and `:154`. §2's proposed "one canonical role vocabulary" would force a merge that the existing design rejects and the two value sets do not align one-to-one (measured/commanded/reference_or_setpoint/status_or_flag/configuration_parameter/derived_or_computed versus measurement/setpoint/state/alarm/command)

findings.reason: §3 must state which existing class absorbs the catalogue form (or that one is replaced by the other), otherwise the live graph carries three shapes for one document.
findings.text: census: `Document` (4311, workflow documented→scored→ingested, `DocumentStatus` at `iter_codex/schemas/common.yaml:222`, readers in `iter_codex/discovery/documents/pipeline.py` and `workers.py`) and `PlantContextDocument` (1884, private and versioned, requires `sha256` and `text`, links `PlantStructure`, written by `iter_codex/discovery/signals/plant_context.py:17`, read by `iter_codex/discovery/signals/group_enrichment.py:89`) are already two document owners with disjoint halves of §4's record; `PlantContextDocument` cannot hold an unfetched document because `sha256` is required, and `Document` has no version, PBS link or version state. §4's "catalogued-document form section 3 introduced" would therefore be a third

findings.reason: the merge of the duplicate memberships is one change across six schema classes and three writers, and §3's "every reader and writer of a changed class uses the new form" is unmeasurable until this census is in the brief.
findings.text: census of the plant-structure and membership owners §2 proposes to revisit: `PlantStructure` (facility.yaml:1855), `PlantSignalRow` (1908, `plant_context.py:270`), `SignalContextLink` (1940, `plant_context.py:391`), `PlantComponent` (1966) with `candidate_plant_component` (facility.yaml:3426) and `archive_component`/`archive_control_node` (3443-3452) as the duplicate pair §1 problem 2 names, plus the three graph writers `plant_context_graph.py:30`, `archive_grouping_graph.py:19` and `group_enrichment.py:74`. Any §3 decision remaps all of these together, and the plan names none

findings.reason: a changed field shape that these readers expose is a public read-path change, and the plan's own gate depends on it.
findings.text: §3's done-when measures "the plant search and signal tools answer the same queries", but `tools/plant_search.py` is the owner of those bounded reads (and `iter_codex/graph/domain_queries.py:124-154` the shared filter builder); §2's review proposes class changes without naming this reader among the ones it must not break

— the section offers a coordinator-supplied record export as an alternative to a client that cannot search; that is a thin layer over a missing capability, and it is WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: either the client gains a bounded search (a real change with a refusal family of its own) or the export is named as the sole route with its provenance recorded; a silent either/or leaves the evidence unverifiable.

findings.reason: §2's verdict vocabulary retires and merges existing classes, so the same account can be extended to the additions at no cost: each new definition states its predecessor or its reason for none.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, §3 and §4 add a catalogue-document form, a document version-state vocabulary that exists nowhere in the shared schema (`superseded` appears only under `iter_codex/schemas/standard_name.yaml:321`), and a control-system-to-PBS binding; neither section names a definition it retires or merges, nor states why nothing can be

findings.reason: the two answer different questions, and only the second keeps the schema from growing a fourth document owner and a third role axis; it costs one clause per proposal.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's single review record with per-class live counts and keep/rename/merge/remove verdicts, plus §3's one migration with a before-image and an idempotency run, is one deep step per endpoint rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3/§4's "catalogued-document form" becomes the third document owner beside `Document` (facility.yaml:4311) and `PlantContextDocument` (facility.yaml:1884), and §4's records search duplicates a client that exists with the capability omitted.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 and §4 add schema definitions (a catalogue-document form, a document version-state vocabulary, a control-system-to-PBS binding) without naming what each retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the endpoints §2 and §4 ask for already have owners in the tree: the field-code table (`iter_codex/discovery/signals/field_codes.py`, `field_codes_graph.py`, `iter_codex/remote/field_code_table.py`) and the document fetch path (`iter_codex/discovery/icp/documents.py:56`), and the plan's §1 problem statements treat both as absent.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's fallback "a record export the coordinator supplies where that client cannot search" is a manual layer around a search the guarded client deliberately refuses to perform.
